newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean union group says strikes to restart Friday.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean union group says strikes to restart Friday.

text.p: South Korea's Korean Confederation of Trade Unions, an outlawed umbrella labour group, has called for strikes to reopen at 9 a.m. (0000 GMT) on Friday, a union official said.
"About 50 unions, totalling about 92,800 members, in the auto making and metal industries, will start striking again this morning," said the official, who declined to be named.
Affiliates of the Hyundai Group, hospital workers and other manufacturers are set to restart their strikes on Monday, he said.
Subway workers are set to walk out again on Tuesday, and will be joined by broadcast workers, he added.

Nationwide strikes erupted on December 26, paralysing major industries, after the ruling New Korea Party rammed a new labour law through parliament that gives employers the right to lay off workers, hire temporary workers and replace strikers.
Strikes were called off for the New Year holidays.
The nation's largest umbrella union group, the Federation of Korean Trade Unions (FKTU), this week called for a suspension of strikes until January 11.
However, the federation warned it would immediately launch strikes again "if the government and employers try to resolve the issue with force".
The FKTU said its second round of strikes would be led by unions in the public and service sectors.
The two umbrella union groups claim an aggregate 1.7 million members in most of South Korea's major industries and public-sector services.
